title: Agent Architecture: ReAct, Planning & Memory Systems
why: A standard LLM is a single-turn autocomplete engine. An AI Agent has agency: it reasons about goals, breaks problems into subtasks, queries tools, observes environmental feedback, updates memory, and adjusts its plan.
objectives: Implement Short-term (buffer), Working (scratchpad), and Long-term (vector) memory
concept: ReAct balances reasoning and action: Reasoning traces help the model induce, track, and update action plans, while actions allow it to interface with external knowledge sources and APIs.

practice.description: Implement a planning step that decomposes a complex user query ('Compare GDP of India and Japan') into two separate search actions.
practice.hint: Return a list of two sub-queries before executing tools.

requirements: Iteratively execute up to 4 research actions, updating working memory at each step
Synthesize citations into a structured Markdown briefing

checklist: Separated short-term scratchpad from persistent long-term storage
mistakes: Allowing the agent to act without reasoning (pure action leads to hallucinated parameters)
